clue.text: The condition of being dejected, having little whisky and gin left?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the state of feeling gloomy

definitions.text: having little whisky and gin left
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: being low on spirits, the drinks

explanation.walkthrough: Whisky and gin are spirits, so a nearly empty drinks cabinet leaves you literally low on spirits; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low-spirited is an idiom for being sad, and the noun names that gloomy state.

clue.text: Will be half queasy when getting funny hat

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters are put into an odd order
only half of the following word is kept, the rest is dropped

explanation.surface: A sick-feeling person cheers up on being given a silly hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name or the future tense but is the verb meaning to leave property by will.
explanation.definitionFit: To will something to a person is to leave it to them in a testament, a synonym.

clue.text: An inducement is to be holding the wife

indicators.note: the outer word grips the other, which sits inside it

parts.note: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a wife is jokingly called one

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hostage, the spouse, as leverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'rib' for a wife comes from the Genesis story and is a familiar crossword joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe is a payment offered to induce someone to act improperly, so it is an inducement.

clue.text: He deals in milk products coming from the main yard

indicators.note: the result emerges out of the source letters, which are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: A farmer sells milk and cheese straight from the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairyman works with or sells milk, butter and cheese, a description of his trade.

clue.text: 101 must go round rising ground to get this hot powder

indicators.note: encircling another word means wrapping around it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: 101 in Roman numerals is C (100) plus I (1)
a hill is ground that rises

explanation.surface: An instruction on a walk: go round the hill to reach the spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' tempts a reversal, but it just describes the ground; the hill is read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli powder is ground dried hot peppers, a fiery spice.

clue.text: They say James splits these showy articles

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound matters

parts.note: Jim is short for James, and to crack is to split

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone called James breaks up flashy ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcracks are cheap, showy ornaments or knick-knacks of little real value.

clue.text: This fair one wants to take half London into an untidy bed

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other
an untidy thing is messed up, so its letters are disordered
only half the city's name is kept

explanation.surface: A fair-haired woman wants to drag half of London into her messy bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair describes light-coloured hair, and a blonde is a person with such hair.

clue.text: How to get a sore bottom, however!

definitions.text: How to get a sore bottom
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read in pieces: by not standing, that is by sitting too long
second meaning: nevertheless, all the same

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into three words and it describes sitting down all day, the cause of a sore bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a preposition or adverb meaning in spite of that, nevertheless.

clue.text: Ovid, half read, leads to sin then separately to go too far

indicators.note: if only half of a name has been read, just its first part is taken

parts.note: the Roman poet; only the first half is kept

explanation.surface: A schoolchild skims half of Ovid's poetry and is led into sin and excess.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to try to do more than one can manage, going beyond one's limits.

clue.text: First person to meet near darkness in a snow house

indicators.note: nearly the whole word means it is one letter short of complete

parts.note: gloom is darkness; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An explorer is the first to meet the polar night inside a snow shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit shelter built from blocks of snow.

clue.text: Move clumsily after Sunday sleep

indicators.note: one part follows the other, so the order of joining is fixed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
to lumber is to move heavily and awkwardly

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles around clumsily after a Sunday lie-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is a literary synonym for sleep.

clue.text: This city in northern India needs success right away

explanation.surface: An Indian city urgently needs success.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh, a state in the north of India.

clue.text: Ruler of Russia, one with vanity half disguised

indicators.note: with half of the word disguised away, only its first part shows

explanation.surface: A tsar whose vanity is only partly concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan was the name of several tsars, notably Ivan the Terrible, ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Live bantam running around, hesitating

indicators.note: a bird running around is all over the place, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A live bantam hen dashes about, unsure which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ambivalent means having mixed feelings, so one is undecided and wavering.

clue.text: Highlight to lay stress on

definitions.meaning: second meaning: put weight on a word or idea

explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean giving something special prominence or importance, the core sense of the verb.

clue.text: Brutal — half-humped one in pub

indicators.note: these parts sit inside the other word
only half of the following word survives

explanation.surface: A violent scene: a hunchbacked figure lurking in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman behaviour lacks compassion, so it is cruel and savage.

clue.text: Money earned as thanks given to monarchs

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Royal income received in gratitude to the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the receipts a shop or business collects, its income.

clue.text: Kind of shirt to make dry

parts.note: as in two and two make four: to total

explanation.surface: Instructions for drying a particular shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' reads as a verb about laundry, but here it is the adjective for no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person or event has no alcohol, and teetotal means abstaining from drink.

clue.text: A period of time when more than eight cravats may be seen?

parts.note: cravats are a kind of tie

explanation.surface: A fashion era when men wore lots of neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineties is a decade, a span of years such as 1990 to 1999.

clue.text: Just so!

parts.note: surface reading: an exclamation of agreement, 'exactly right'
setter's reading: fair and impartial, an adjective, with 'so' adding emphasis

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like someone nodding along, but 'just' is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone even-handed treats all sides equally, which is what being just means.

clue.text: Don't start sending the denouement

indicators.note: refusing to start means the first letter is left off

explanation.surface: An author is told to hold back the final chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A denouement is the final resolution of a story, its conclusion.

clue.text: Name of chocolate found in bed, half left

indicators.note: only half of the next word is kept

parts.note: a nest is a bird's bed

explanation.surface: A chocolate bar discovered half-eaten in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestlé is a large Swiss food company famous for its chocolate brand.

clue.text: Old sovereign in Peru, somewhat incapable

indicators.note: only some of the next word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A former Peruvian ruler who was rather useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca was the emperor of the Inca empire based in Peru.

clue.text: Game where Mr Crosby gained nothing

explanation.surface: A game in which the crooner Crosby won nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance played by marking off called numbers on a card.

clue.text: Nuts cracked by Sid in turn for those undressed

indicators.note: a nut cracked open lets something into its middle
turning a name round makes it read the other way

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Sid takes his turn cracking nuts at a gathering of naturists.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists choose to go without clothes, so they are people unclothed.

clue.text: Left out "glove" in a famous English dictionary

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

explanation.surface: The word glove has been dropped from a famous dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out or excluded, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Music is no good when found in an urgent message

indicators.note: something found inside sits within the outer word

parts.note: a common abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A distress call mocking some bad music.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs are pieces of vocal music, so the plural stands for music in general.

clue.text: Which colour makes you feel anger?

indicators.note: what you make is built anew, so the letters are formed into another word

explanation.surface: A question about which colour makes you furious, seeing red perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaf-green is the bright green shade of foliage, a colour.
